<div class="eyebrow">BIOSTATISTICS · STATISTICAL COMPUTING · PUBLIC HEALTH</div>

## Learning to turn data into understanding.

I'm **Mingcan Li**, an ScM student at the **Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health**. My current coursework brings together biostatistics, probability, statistical computing, and epidemiology.

This website is part of **Project 0 for Statistical Computing (BSPH 140.776)** and a home for my developing work in R.

<div class="links">
[GitHub profile](https://github.com/Mingcan-li)
[Course website](https://lcolladotor.github.io/jhustatcomputing/)
</div>

## Current learning

### Statistical foundations

Through **Methods in Biostatistics I** and **Essentials of Probability and Statistical Inference I: Probability**, I'm building a foundation in statistical methods, uncertainty, and inference.

### Computing and reproducibility

In **Statistical Computing**, I'm learning to use R, RStudio, tidyverse, R Markdown, Git, and GitHub to organize analyses and communicate results. My current focus is developing a reproducible workflow and becoming more comfortable with programming.

### Public health context

**Epidemiologic Inference in Public Health I**, **Foundational Principles of Public Health**, and **Introduction to the Biomedical Sciences I** connect my quantitative coursework with questions about population health. **Current Topics in Biostatistics Research** introduces me to research directions in the field.

## Building experience

I'm currently developing my statistical and programming skills through coursework. Project 0 brings several pieces of that learning together: setting up an R environment, using Git and GitHub, and creating a website from R Markdown.

## Goals for Statistical Computing

- Become more confident writing and understanding R code.
- Practice data exploration and clear visualization.
- Create reproducible reports that combine code, results, and explanation.
- Use Git and GitHub to track changes and share projects.
